DESCRIPTION

  Meridian Credits quotes loyalty credits for a subscription reseller. The    
  local Python CLI accepts one JSON object on stdin and emits exactly one JSON
  object on stdout; run python3 main.py. Preserve {"command":"ping"} ->       
  {"status":"ok","product":"Meridian Credits"} and the existing unknown-      
  command response. No network, clock, locale or third-party package is       
  needed. Malformed input is outside these issues.                            
                                                                              
  A charge line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on, 
  and charge_cents. The three IDs are nonempty strings; line_id is unique     
  within a request. A subscription is identified by the pair (account_id,     
  subscription_id); the same subscription_id can occur under different        
  accounts, and a subscription can have several charge lines. service_on is a 
  valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31.         
  charge_cents is a nonnegative integer in US cents. No line is excluded by   
  its service date. Each request is the complete charge set of one            
  independently quoted monthly statement; caps apply within that set. Line    
  collections may be empty. Lexicographic ID order means Unicode code-point   
  order. JSON object key order is immaterial; do not add response keys beyond 
  those specified.                                                            
                                                                              
  Release "1.0" is the initial agreement. An omitted release selects the      
  current agreement; an explicit supported release selects that version.      
  Versions introduced in an issue remain supported afterward. Public suites   
  name a specific release and send explicit release values, so their          
  expectations remain applicable when the current agreement changes. Run a    
  supplied suite with python3 test_public.py --cases PATH.                    
                                                                              
  Add statement to display the credit assigned to every line under the current
  approved agreement. Request: {"command":"statement","lines":[LINE,...]} with
  optional release "2.0". Return exactly release, lines, credit_cents, and    
  amount_due_cents. Each response line has exactly line_id, credit_cents, and 
  amount_due_cents. Preserve the input line order in the response. Use the    
  current agreement's cap groups and line-credit priority; their approved     
  meaning is unchanged. Overall amounts equal total for the same input.       
                                                                              
  Empty input returns release "2.0", lines [], and both totals zero. One-line 
  example response: {"release": "2.0", "credit_cents": 2999,                  
  "amount_due_cents": 17000, "lines": [{"line_id": "L-1", "credit_cents":     
  2999, "amount_due_cents": 17000}]}. Existing quote and total release support
  is unchanged.

Meridian Credits release "2.0" credit agreement (Finance-approved and permanently adopted as the CURRENT agreement, per issue trial-a6r; supersedes release 1.0 as current). Applies to every supplied charge set regardless of service dates. An omitted release now selects "2.0"; explicit "2.0" behaves identically; explicit "1.0" still uses the original agreement (see key meridian-credits/release-1.0-credit-agreement). Rules: (1) uncapped line credit = 15% of charge_cents, floored per line to integer cents; (2) credit cap 3000 cents shared by all lines with the same (account_id, subscription_id) pair; distinct pairs have independent caps (same subscription_id under different accounts = different groups); (3) within a cap group, priority = largest charge_cents first, ties by increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order); service_on never affects priority; each line gets its uncapped credit up to the remaining cap, later lines get the remainder or zero; (4) total credit = sum of line credits; line amount_due = charge - credit; total due = total charges - total credit. Request/response shapes unchanged from 1.0: quote {"command":"quote","line":LINE[,"release":R]} -> exactly {release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; total {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...][,"release":R]} -> exactly {release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; the response release identifies the agreement actually used; unsupported release -> {"error":"unsupported_release"}. Example: quote L-1 charge 19999 with omitted release -> {"release":"2.0","credit_cents":2999,"amount_due_cents":17000,"line_id":"L-1"}. Implementation: main.py RELEASES table holds per-release rate_percent, cap_cents, cap_group key, and priority sort key; CURRENT_RELEASE = "2.0"; assign_credits(lines, rules) is the shared cap/priority engine. Public suite: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/release_2_quote_total.json (release 1 suites remain applicable and must keep passing).

Meridian Credits release "1.0" credit agreement (Finance-approved, per issue trial-4tt). HISTORICAL: as of issue trial-a6r, release 1.0 is no longer the current agreement; an omitted release now selects "2.0" (see key meridian-credits/release-2.0-credit-agreement). Release 1.0 remains supported and is used only when a request sends explicit "release":"1.0". Rules: (1) uncapped line credit = 10% of charge_cents, floored per line to integer cents; (2) credit cap 2400 cents shared by all lines with the same account_id across its subscriptions, independent per account; (3) within a cap group, priority = earliest service_on first, ties by increasing line_id (Unicode code-point order); each line gets its uncapped credit up to the remaining cap, later lines get the remainder or zero; (4) total credit = sum of line credits; line amount_due = charge - credit; total due = total charges - total credit. Data model: line has exactly line_id, account_id, subscription_id, service_on (YYYY-MM-DD, 2020-01-01..2099-12-31), charge_cents (nonneg int); subscription key is (account_id, subscription_id); caps apply within one request. Quote command: {"command":"quote","line":LINE,"release":"1.0"} -> exactly {release, line_id, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; single line is treated as the whole statement. Total command (issue trial-fjv): {"command":"total","lines":[LINE,...],"release":"1.0"} -> exactly {release, credit_cents, amount_due_cents}; caps apply across the whole supplied set, not per line; empty lines -> credit 0, due 0. Implementation: main.py RELEASES["1.0"] entry (rate_percent 10, cap_cents 2400, cap_group account_id, priority (service_on, line_id)); assign_credits(lines, rules) runs the cap/priority engine; quote() and total() both call it. Public suites: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/release_1_quote.json and public_tests/release_1_total.json.
